name: ControlledChaos
description: An ADHD-friendly task manager built around brain dumps (text, voice, or photo) that Claude Haiku parses into structured tasks. Crisis mode for overwhelm days, AI-powered prioritization that factors in time and energy, and Parallel Play rooms for body-doubling with friends. One-tap Moments capture energy and focus state; microtasks surface small recurring prompts without streak guilt. Includes Canvas calendar sync, location-aware notifications, momentum visualization, and a Mirror view that shows your whole day in one chronological timeline. Targeting public launch June 2026.

name: ChaosLimbă
tagline: English-to-Romanian language learning grounded in SLA research.
description: A CALL app for English speakers learning Romanian, designed for ADHD brains and grounded in second language acquisition theory. Built around a 10-component AI ensemble with fossilization detection that turns persistent errors into micro-curriculum. Targeting MVP launch August 2026.

name: ChaosLengua
description: Spanish-language sister project to ChaosLimbă, built in a shared monorepo with the same SLA-grounded AI ensemble architecture and Adaptation Engine. Shares Clerk auth and monorepo tooling with ChaosLimbă while targeting Spanish-specific error patterns like ser/estar and preterite/imperfect.

name: ChaosPatch
tagline: Patch tracker built for agentic development workflows.
description: A PWA for tracking dev patches — small specs that Claude Code can pick up and implement. Integrated via MCP so patches flow directly into Claude Code sessions instead of dying in a Notion doc. Attach screenshots to a patch and Claude sees them as visual context. Includes batch updates, cross-project search, tag filtering, and an Insights page that visualizes work-in-flight across projects.

name: ScribeCat
description: Records lectures with real-time AssemblyAI transcription, generates AI study notes mid-recording (not after), and includes six AI study tools (flashcards, quizzes, concept maps, ELI5). Features exam study rooms with weak-spot tracking, a Tamagotchi-style pixel cat (StudyQuest) tied to study metrics, multiplayer Quiz Battle and Jeopardy, friends + DMs, and a Chrome extension that imports Canvas courses.

name: ThreadNotes
tagline: Personal research command center for the way ADHD brains actually research.
description: A unified hub for academic research: search peer-reviewed literature via OpenAlex and Crossref, automatically discover free open-access PDFs via Unpaywall, save and annotate articles, organize research questions by theme with bidirectional article linking, write reflective journal entries, and get AI-generated summaries. Includes a Chrome extension for clipping excerpts and an MCP server so Claude can read and write to your research base.

name: ThreadBrain
tagline: Reading companion that scaffolds dense text for ADHD brains.
description: AI-generated micro-headers, purpose-aware chunking that adapts to your stated reading goal and energy level, and "The Map" — a 2-3 sentence orientation summary before reading begins. Includes ExpressBrain for cram-sheet generation and integrates with ThreadNotes so excerpts flow into your research thread.

name: ChickenScratch
tagline: Editorial portal for Hen & Ink Society literary zine.
description: The submissions and review portal for Hen & Ink Society, the first AAP-based RSO at the University of Delaware. Handles submission intake, editor review, and publishing workflows for the zine.

name: Personal Context MCP
description: An MCP server that stores identity, projects, relationships, and preferences for cross-session Claude context. Powers Cha(t)os context awareness and provides continuity across Claude conversations. Multi-tenant with Redis-backed persistence.

name: Tangle
description: An MCP server that persists Claude's epistemic state across sessions — hunches, suspicions, dead-ends, and partial reasoning that would otherwise evaporate at session end. Sibling to Personal Context MCP (which captures identity and projects) and the built-in memory feature (which captures chat history); Tangle captures the texture of working on a problem. Each Claude attributes their notes via an identity header or URL parameter, and a recency × confidence ranking surfaces what matters most when re-entering a project.

name: Songs of My Selves: We as Walt
tagline: Walk through Whitman's *Song of Myself* amid a network of stars.
description: An interactive map of Walt Whitman's Epic-like *Song of Myself*. All 52 sections are paired with songs that match the emotions and themes they contain. Click any star in the constellation to read the section in full and listen to its accompanying track. The constellation lives inside a deep-space scene — drifting nebula clouds, a parallax starfield that shifts with depth as you pan and zoom, and the occasional shooting star.

name: LibraLex
tagline: Your shelf, your wishlist, your library loans — plus the next book you'll love, recommended by friends and the catalog.
description: A personal book catalog that tracks the three states a book actually lives in — owned, wished-for, and borrowed-from-the-library (with due dates so nothing goes overdue). Search or scan a title to pull clean covers, summaries, subjects, and author bios from Google Books and Open Library. It learns from the books you've read and rated to suggest what to read next — pulling not just from your own shelves but from your friends' shelves and the wider Open Library catalog, every pick explained ('because you loved X', 'Maya loved this', 'popular in fantasy') and never a black box. Recommendations run on real semantic understanding under the hood (every book is embedded and matched to your taste by meaning, not keyword overlap), and you can just ask in plain language — 'something atmospheric and slow' — to search your friends' shelves for a vibe instead of a title. Beyond the made-for-you picks, you can go exploring on your own terms — browse popular books in the genres you choose, and open any author's full catalog with a tap on their name — and when you spot one you want, every book is one tap from a used copy on ThriftBooks. A friends layer lets you swap shelves and trade recommendations, with per-shelf privacy controls so you decide exactly what friends can see, and an MCP server lets Claude run your whole shelf from chat — not just 'what am I reading?' and 'what's due soon?', but 'I finished Dune, five stars', 'add The Hobbit to my shelf', 'I returned my library book', 'what should I read next?', and 'recommend it to Maya', all in plain conversation.

name: Kindling
tagline: A place for ideas to catch before they go out.
description: An MCP-connected store for sparks and half-formed ideas — capture, dig back through, archive, or promote them into real projects. Exposed to Claude via kindle/kindling_* tools.

name: The Majorot
tagline: A solo tarot journaling RPG, played with a real deck and tracked in-app.
description: A companion app for a physical solo journaling RPG: draw through a real tarot deck one sitting at a time, collecting all 22 Major Arcana spells before the deck runs out. Majors are spells, Court cards are allies or duel opponents, and Pips are life events — combat runs on a d6 and an elemental rock-paper-scissors wheel (Fire/Water/Air/Earth). The app tracks Self & Spark, allies, kit items, and an editable journal offline-first via IndexedDB, with a full in-app rules reference and round-by-round combat log. Engine logic (122 passing tests) is traceable line-by-line to the written rulebook.

name: ChaosLingua Lite
description: A lighter-weight companion app in the Chaos language-learning family, focused on Latin curriculum and drills.

name: Color Factory
description: Lock the colors you want to keep, pick a harmony style, and let an OKLCH engine fill the rest — then export a polished, shareable palette card as PNG or SVG.

name: DuelingChaos
tagline: A Magic: The Gathering client built on a real rules engine.
description: A headless integration with Forge, the open-source MTG rules engine, bridged over HTTP as a JSON game-state API — full stack/targeting/static-ability resolution rather than a simplified simulation. The React frontend renders live board state with stack visualization and targeting arrows, a complete choice UI (targeting, modal spells, mana payment, X-costs, multi-blocker combat damage assignment), and a deckbuilder with card search, legality checking, and save/load.

name: FeyForge
description: A D&D 5e companion built with Next.js and Convex: full character sheets across the 2014 and 2024 rules, live real-time sessions with synced audio and live captions, an interactive world map, a campaign wiki, homebrew authoring, an AI DM assistant, a friends/social layer, and AI-assisted character & NPC building.

name: Loose Change
description: Voice/text capture for stray thoughts that hit while driving, falling asleep, or otherwise mid-task — the ones that aren't ControlledChaos tasks and aren't Kindling-worthy sparks. Talk or type, release, triage later in batches.

name: Stellation
description: Takes birth data, calculates a real natal chart via Skyfield and JPL's DE440s ephemeris, and renders it as generative art with an AI-generated interpretation. Beyond a solo natal chart: synastry, composite charts, transits, and solar/Saturn returns, with optional sign-in to save and revisit charts.

name: Syzygy
description: Every reading draws Major Arcana weighted by your input and today's actual planetary transits, then renders live as a unique constellation — no two readings ever look the same, because the sky itself has changed since last time.
